svg.data-cluster-capacity: up to 691 Tb/s in an S9700-series DDC cluster
svg.data-circuit-reserve: 2000 W recommended on each of two feeds
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD SR8, LR8, DR4 and FR4; 400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AEC and AOC (datasheet Compatible Fabric Transceiver Types and Compatible Fabric Cable Types)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: NOT PUBLISHED FOR THESE PORTS. The datasheet's Compatible Fabric Transceiver Types and Compatible Fabric Cable Types blocks cover the forty-eight QSFP-DD fabric ports only; no held document names a single optic for the two 10G SFP+ management ports, which the port list describes as '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports' and nothing more. The cages are drawn to the SFP/SFP+ standard on that description
svg.data-fabric-only: the forty-eight QSFP-DD ports are CELL-BASED fabric ports and the guide says they 'should only be used to interconnect with other fabric ports of the S9700 series' - they are not general Ethernet ports
svg.data-cell-switching: cell-based switching eliminates Ethernet overhead and load-balances every fabric link, at 8 billion cells per second, with internal data-cell memory
svg.data-ddc: backplane switch fabric for a Distributed Disaggregated Chassis built from S9700-series routers, scaling horizontally in a pay-as-you-grow model
svg.data-console: RJ45 serial console and micro USB, both legended IOIO on the faceplate; 115200 8N1, no parity, no flow control (HIG Initial System Setup). The micro USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver
svg.data-oob: 1x RJ45 100/1000M out-of-band management port with link and activity lamps
svg.data-boot-time: approximately 110 s from power-on and 40 s for the OOB port to link, both measured on Ubuntu Linux and NOS-dependent (HIG NEBS statements)
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; RCM AS/NZS CISPR 32, Class A; Anatel

circle.data-description: HIG section 10, Fan FRU LED table - Off (BMC is not up), Green (fan FRU function normal), Amber (fan FRU is abnormal, the fan speed is under 4500 rpm). Three rows and no blink states; transcribed as it stands rather than filled out from a sibling guide's longer table

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)
